cpu_contract.scope: Instruction-success effects only. No source types, services, memory validity, segment bases, ABI preservation or completed runtime path is established.
cpu_contract.initial_state: Use actual current ESP/SS for the entry load; all prior register, flags, segment-descriptor, memory and provider state remains unknown. Explicit ESP-based address size is 32 bits without establishing implicit stack size.
cpu_contract.local_stack_predicates: Renew actual current SS.B=1 separately at each PUSH, POP, CALL and RET when using ESP +/-4 formulas. Without that predicate, these formulas are not asserted; the actual SS descriptor selects the implicit stack address size.

local_branches.predicate: SF != OF from the immediately preceding ECX-ESI CMP; after the local successful XOR ESI,ESI and no intervening state change, this is signed ECX < 0
ZF==1 or SF!=OF from ECX-2; along the preceding local nonnegative edge, this selects ECX 0..2
ZF==0 from ECX-3; along the preceding local >2 edge, unequal values select C26B80 and equality selects C26B6C

cpu_contract.local_absolute_access_routes: The local 0..2 edge reads a dword through current DS:0109DDD0 into EAX and writes current ECX to that same encoded offset, then executes POP ESI/RET. The local equality-to-3 edge reads that offset into EAX then POP ESI/RET. These are physical schedules; no cell ownership, global type or service name is inferred.

first_opaque_boundary.claim: No destination query. If execution returns to C26B85, renew all actual current state; zero ESI from before the opaque callee is not assumed to survive.

cpu_contract.post_first_call_schedule: Five PUSH ESI instructions use their actual current ESI and SS stack state. They are not authenticated zero arguments. The following C26B8A store writes immediate22 through current DS:[EAX], with no returned-pointer or provider interpretation. Stack, absolute-cell and indirect-store aliases are not excluded.

second_opaque_boundary.claim: No destination query. Any actual return state is opaque, including ESP, ESI, EBP, flags, DS/SS descriptors and memory.

cpu_contract.post_second_call_schedule: C26B95 adds20 to actual current ESP and derives arithmetic flags; it is not proof that five earlier arguments were removed. C26B98 then makes EAX=FFFFFFFF, CF=OF=0, SF=PF=1, ZF=0, AF undefined on successful completion. The subsequent local POP ESI and near RET do not modify EAX or those flags on normal completion; they use renewed current SS/stack predicates and actual stack contents, with an unknown return destination. This is not a proved completed whole-function path.
cpu_contract.preservation_limits: An earlier PUSH and later POP do not alone prove ESI preservation: unknown callees, stack changes, SS descriptor changes and possible aliasing stores can invalidate that conclusion. Near RET reads its actual current stack destination, without authenticating the original return slot.
